definitions.explanation: a mechanical or structural arrangement designed to achieve a specific effect
a clever plan or arrangement designed to produce a desired outcome

examples.japanese: この{時計|とけい}には{複雑|ふくざつ}な{仕掛|しか}けがある。
examples.english: This clock has a complex mechanism.

examples.japanese: マジックの{仕掛|しか}けがわからない。
examples.english: I can't figure out the trick behind the magic.

examples.japanese: {仕掛|しか}け{絵本|えほん}を{買|か}った。
この{映画|えいが}には{意外|いがい}な{仕掛|しか}けがある。
examples.english: This movie has a surprising twist.

examples.japanese: {罠|わな}の{仕掛|しか}けを{解除|かいじょ}した。
この{事件|じけん}には{何|なに}か{仕掛|しか}けがあるはずだ。
examples.english: There must be some trick behind this incident.

notes:
{仕掛|しか}け refers to mechanisms, devices, or clever setups.

ETYMOLOGY:
- From {仕掛|しか}ける (to set up, to set a trap)
- {仕|し}: To do
- {掛|か}け: To hang, to set

SENSE 1 VS SENSE 2:
- Sense 1: Physical mechanisms (clocks, toys, traps)
- Sense 2: Abstract tricks or setups (plots, magic tricks)

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {仕掛|しか}け{絵本|えほん} (pop-up book)
- {仕掛|しか}け{花火|はなび} (fireworks display)
- {仕掛|しか}け{時計|どけい} (mechanical clock with figures)
- からくり{仕掛|しか}け (elaborate mechanism)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {仕掛|しか}けがある (to have a mechanism/trick)
- {仕掛|しか}けを{作|つく}る (to create a mechanism)
- {仕掛|しか}けを{見破|みやぶ}る (to see through a trick)
- {罠|わな}の{仕掛|しか}け (trap mechanism)

RELATED VERB:
- {仕掛|しか}ける (to set up, to start, to attack)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- からくり (mechanism - traditional)
- トリック (trick - loanword)
- {装置|そうち} (device - more technical)

REGISTER: Neutral. Common in everyday conversation.
